chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: A molecule of glucose is completely oxidised in aerobic respiration and molecules of \(H_2O\) and ____ are produced along with energy.
solution: In aerobic respiration one molecule of glucose is completely oxidised in the presence of oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water along with energy (ATP): \(C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O + \text{energy}\). Hence, along with water, \(CO_2\) is produced. Oxygen is used up (not produced), so the answer is \(CO_2\).

stem: Vinegar contains ____ acid.
solution: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid. It is produced by acetic acid bacteria (Acetobacter aceti), which oxidise the ethanol of a fermented liquid into acetic acid. Lactic acid is formed by Lactobacillus in curd, so the correct answer is acetic acid.

stem: Any nucleotide of the gene suddenly changes its position that causes a minor change which is nothing but the ____.
solution: A sudden change in the sequence or position of a nucleotide of a gene (DNA) is called a mutation. Mutations bring about heritable variations. Translocation is a specific type of chromosomal aberration, but the general term for such a minor change in a nucleotide is mutation.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: In humans, sperm production occurs in the ____ organ.
solution: Sperms (male gametes) are produced in the testes, in the seminiferous tubules, by the process of spermatogenesis (meiosis). The vas deferens and ejaculatory duct only carry the sperms; they do not produce them. Hence the answer is testes.

stem: Solar photovoltaic cell converts the solar radiation energy directly into ____ energy.
solution: A solar photovoltaic (PV) cell is made of semiconductor material that directly converts the energy of solar radiation (sunlight) into electrical energy by the photovoltaic effect. Hence the answer is electrical energy.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Find the odd one out: Fragmentation, Regeneration, Budding, Fertilization.
solution: Fertilization is the odd one out. Fragmentation, regeneration and budding are all methods of asexual reproduction (a single parent, no gamete fusion), whereas fertilization is the fusion of male and female gametes and is a part of sexual reproduction.

stem: Write the correct co-relation: Diabetes : Insulin :: Cancer : ____
solution: Cancer : Interferon. Just as diabetes is treated using the hormone insulin (produced by biotechnology / genetic engineering), cancer is treated using interferon, an anti-cancer/anti-viral protein produced by recombinant DNA technology.

stem: State whether true or false: Study of fossils is an important aspect of the study of evolution.
solution: True. Fossils are the preserved remains or impressions of organisms that lived in the past. Their study (palaeontology) gives direct evidence of evolution — the age, form and gradual changes of extinct organisms — and hence is an important aspect of the study of evolution.

stem: Give any two commercial uses of Biotechnology.
solution: Two commercial uses of biotechnology: (1) Production of medicines and biomolecules such as insulin, interferon, vaccines, antibiotics and hormones by recombinant DNA technology. (2) Production of genetically modified (GM) crops with higher yield and resistance to pests/diseases, e.g. Bt cotton. (Other uses: production of enzymes, biofertilizers and improved products in the food and dairy industry.)

stem: Being a fish, I perform respiration with the help of lungs. Who am I?
solution: I am a lungfish (e.g. Protopterus / Neoceratodus). Although it is a fish (class Pisces), the lungfish can breathe air using lung-like structures in addition to gills; it is regarded as a connecting link between fishes and amphibians.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Give scientific reason: Sometimes, higher plants and animals too perform anaerobic respiration.
solution: Higher plants and animals normally respire aerobically, but when the supply of oxygen becomes insufficient, their cells switch to anaerobic respiration to obtain energy. For example, the roots of plants in waterlogged soil and human muscle cells during vigorous exercise do not get enough oxygen; so glucose is broken down incompletely without oxygen — muscles form lactic acid, and plant cells form ethanol and \(CO_2\). Thus, under low-oxygen conditions, higher plants and animals too perform anaerobic respiration.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Give scientific reason: It is not right to consider the mother responsible for giving birth to a girl child.
solution: The sex of a child is determined by the sex chromosome contributed by the father, not the mother. A woman has \(XX\) sex chromosomes, so all her eggs carry only an X chromosome. A man has \(XY\), so his sperms are of two kinds — X-bearing and Y-bearing. If an X-bearing sperm fertilises the egg, the child is a girl \((XX)\); if a Y-bearing sperm does so, the child is a boy \((XY)\). Since the mother can give only X and it is the father's sperm that decides the sex, it is scientifically wrong to blame the mother for the birth of a girl child.

stem: Give scientific reason: The energy generated from nuclear fuels is not environment friendly.
solution: Nuclear power stations produce highly radioactive waste which remains dangerous for thousands of years and is very difficult to store and dispose of safely. Any leakage of radiation or a reactor accident can cause radiation sickness, cancers, genetic disorders and death of living organisms, and the hot water released causes thermal pollution. Because of this radioactive waste and the risk of radiation hazards, the energy generated from nuclear fuels is not environment friendly.

stem: Complete the following food chain: Grass \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) Eagle \(\rightarrow\) ____
solution: The completed food chain: Grass \(\rightarrow\) Grasshopper \(\rightarrow\) Frog \(\rightarrow\) Snake \(\rightarrow\) Eagle \(\rightarrow\) Decomposers (microorganisms). Here grass is the producer, the grasshopper is the primary (herbivore) consumer, the frog is the secondary consumer, the snake is the tertiary consumer, the eagle is the top carnivore, and on its death the decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down the dead matter. (Other acceptable herbivore/carnivore pairs, e.g. insect / lizard, are also valid.)

stem: Distinguish between the following: Class Pisces and Class Reptiles.
solution:
| Class Pisces | Class Reptilia |
|---|---|
| Body is streamlined and covered with mucus-coated scales. | Body is covered with dry, horny, keratinised scales or scutes. |
| Respiration takes place only through gills. | Respiration takes place only through lungs. |
| They are aquatic (live in water). | They are mostly terrestrial (some are aquatic but breathe air). |
| Heart is two-chambered. | Heart is incompletely three-chambered. |
| Fertilization is usually external and eggs are laid in water. | Fertilization is internal and shelled eggs are laid on land. |
Examples: Pisces — Labeo (rohu), Scoliodon; Reptilia — lizard, snake, tortoise.

stem: Observe the following picture and write any two effects of this disaster.
solution: The picture shows a flood (a low-lying area, road and railway track submerged under water with people wading through it). Two effects of a flood: (1) Loss of human and animal life and large-scale damage to houses, crops, roads, railways and other property. (2) Contamination of drinking-water sources leading to the spread of waterborne diseases such as cholera, typhoid and gastroenteritis, along with disruption of transport, electricity and communication.

stem: Write any four methods to reduce stress.
solution: Four methods to reduce stress: (1) Perform regular exercise, yoga, meditation and deep-breathing (pranayama). (2) Take proper rest and adequate sound sleep and eat a balanced, nutritious diet. (3) Engage in hobbies and recreational activities such as music, reading, sports and gardening. (4) Share your problems and feelings with family and friends, and take help/counselling from elders or experts when needed. (Also: proper time management and maintaining a positive attitude.)

stem: Complete the following conceptual picture (uses of 'Sewage after processing' — four uses around the central box).
solution: Uses of sewage (waste water) after processing / treatment: (1) For irrigation of fields in agriculture. (2) For gardening and maintaining green landscapes/parks. (3) For industrial purposes, such as cooling and cleaning in industries and thermal power plants. (4) For recharging groundwater and for non-drinking domestic uses such as flushing toilets, washing and construction work. (Treated water thus conserves fresh water and prevents pollution of rivers.)

stem: Define heredity. Explain the mechanism of hereditary changes.
solution: Heredity: Heredity is the transmission of characters (traits) from parents to their offspring through genes, generation after generation. Mechanism of hereditary changes: A gene is a specific segment of DNA that controls a particular character. During reproduction, genes are passed from parents to offspring. Hereditary changes (variations) arise mainly in two ways — (a) Mutation: a sudden change in the sequence or position of the nucleotides of a gene alters the character it controls; and (b) Recombination: the reshuffling and new combinations of parental genes during meiosis and sexual reproduction. Such changes, if they occur in the gametes, are inherited by the next generation and, over long periods, accumulate to bring about evolution. Thus genes carry heredity, and changes in genes are the basis of hereditary variation.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Write any four stages of mitosis and explain any two of them.
solution: The four stages (of karyokinesis) in mitosis are: (1) Prophase, (2) Metaphase, (3) Anaphase, (4) Telophase. Explanation of any two: (a) Prophase — the chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes, each seen as two sister chromatids joined at the centromere; the nuclear membrane and nucleolus gradually disappear and the spindle fibres begin to form. (b) Metaphase — the chromosomes arrange themselves in a single row at the equatorial plane (equator) of the cell and the spindle fibres get attached to the centromere of each chromosome. (Anaphase — the centromeres split and the sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles; Telophase — the chromosomes reach the poles, uncoil, and two new nuclear membranes form giving two daughter nuclei.)

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Explain with examples types of asexual reproduction in unicellular organism.
solution: Types of asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms: (1) Binary fission — the parent cell divides into two equal daughter cells, e.g. Amoeba, Paramoecium, bacteria. (2) Multiple fission — the nucleus divides repeatedly and the cell splits into many daughter cells at once, e.g. Plasmodium (malarial parasite). (3) Budding — a small outgrowth (bud) develops on the parent, grows and separates to form a new individual, e.g. yeast. (4) Spore formation — special reproductive cells (spores) are produced which germinate into new individuals, e.g. some algae and fungi. In all these, a single parent produces genetically identical offspring without the fusion of gametes.

stem: Which fuel is used in thermal power plant? Write any two problems associated with this type of power generation.
solution: Fuel used in a thermal power plant: coal (fossil fuel); some plants also use oil or natural gas. Two problems associated with thermal power generation: (1) Burning of coal releases large amounts of \(CO_2\), oxides of sulphur and nitrogen, smoke and ash, causing air pollution, global warming and acid rain. (2) Coal is a non-renewable (exhaustible) fossil fuel whose reserves are limited and getting depleted, and disposal of the huge quantity of ash produced is also a problem.

stem: Write three characteristics of phylum-Mollusca.
solution: Three characteristics of phylum Mollusca: (1) The body is soft and unsegmented, and is usually protected by a hard calcareous shell. (2) A muscular foot is present which is used for locomotion (and in some for capturing food). (3) A soft skin fold called the mantle covers the visceral mass and secretes the shell; the body shows bilateral symmetry and organ-system level of organisation. Examples: snail (Pila), mussel, octopus.

stem: What are the constituents of acid rain? What are its two effects on earth's surface?
solution: Constituents of acid rain: acid rain mainly contains sulphuric acid \((H_2SO_4)\) and nitric acid \((HNO_3)\). These are formed when oxides of sulphur \((SO_2)\) and oxides of nitrogen \((NO_x)\) — released by burning of fossil fuels — dissolve in rain water. Two effects on earth's surface: (1) It makes the soil and water bodies (lakes, rivers) acidic, which harms crops, plants, aquatic animals and reduces soil fertility. (2) It corrodes and damages buildings, bridges, metal structures and marble monuments (e.g. the Taj Mahal).

stem: Write down the reasons, effects and remedial measures taken for any one disaster seen or heard by you.
solution: Disaster: Flood. Reasons: heavy and continuous rainfall, overflowing of rivers, breaching or failure of dams, blocked or poor drainage, and deforestation which reduces the soil's capacity to hold water. Effects: loss of human and animal life; damage to houses, roads, railways, crops and property; contamination of drinking water leading to epidemics of waterborne diseases; and disruption of electricity, transport and communication. Remedial measures: timely warning and evacuation of people to safe places; setting up relief camps providing food, clean water and medicines; construction of embankments/dams and proper drainage systems; afforestation to control run-off; and rehabilitation and financial help to the affected people. (Any one disaster — flood, earthquake, cyclone, landslide — with its reasons, effects and remedies is acceptable.)

stem: What is biodiversity? Write any four steps to conserve biodiversity.
solution: Biodiversity: Biodiversity is the variety and variability among all the living organisms — plants, animals and microorganisms — present in a particular region or ecosystem, including the diversity of genes, species and ecosystems. Four steps to conserve biodiversity: (1) In-situ conservation — protecting organisms in their natural habitats by setting up national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves. (2) Ex-situ conservation — protecting them outside their habitat in zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks and gene banks. (3) Preventing deforestation and habitat destruction and promoting afforestation. (4) Imposing a strict ban on poaching and illegal trade of wild plants and animals and creating public awareness about conservation. (Also: controlling pollution and preventing over-exploitation of natural resources.)

stem: What is stem cell? Write any four uses of stem cell.
solution: Stem cell: Stem cells are unspecialised (undifferentiated) cells of the body that have the ability to divide repeatedly and to differentiate into various specialised types of cells and tissues. Four uses of stem cells: (1) In regenerative medicine / stem-cell therapy to repair or replace damaged tissues and organs. (2) In the treatment of blood disorders through bone-marrow transplantation, e.g. leukaemia (blood cancer) and thalassaemia. (3) For growing tissues and organs in the laboratory for transplantation and for treating burns by skin grafting. (4) In the treatment of degenerative diseases such as diabetes, Parkinson's disease, paralysis and spinal-cord injuries, and in research on drug testing and disease study.
